correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\) and odd \(m\ge n\), the oriented wedge has an inward-pointing boundary, and \(\dot z\ge Kz^{m+1}\) forces finite maximal time. Bounded \(z\) is incompatible with finite-time loss of the solution by Gronwall. Integrating \(dv/dz=b(sz)-z^{2n-1}/v\) establishes \(v=Az^{m+1}+Qz^{m-1}+o(z^{m-1})\), with the restoring contribution at this order exactly when \(m=n\). The exact remaining-time integral \(T-t=\int_z^\infty d\zeta/v(\zeta)\) and asymptotic inversion give both physical-time coefficients, including the sign and \(m+2\) denominator. Finite coefficient tests supplement, but cannot replace, the proof for the entire stated range. Nothing is claimed about orbits outside the open escape wedge.

value.rationale: The original global-center question distinguishes periodic from non-global motion but does not determine maximal physical-time lifespan or sharp escape observables. An explicit open sector yields a whole family, not an isolated solution, with an initial-data-independent exponent and genuinely two-term quantitative law. The equality \(m=n\) is the structural threshold at which restoring force first enters the subleading term, distinguishing naturally different degree regimes rather than an arbitrary slice.
